title: Grožnjan Cost Guide 2027: Prices for Stay, Food, Parking
metaDescription: Grožnjan costs in euros for 2027: rooms from about €50–90, konoba meals €15–35, truffle products, parking, and day-trip budgets for this Istrian hill town.
content:
## How Much Does a Trip to Grožnjan Cost?

Grožnjan is a small hilltop town in northwest Istria with about 20 galleries and artist studios, and it is cheaper than the coast around Rovinj or Poreč. Budget travelers can manage a day trip for roughly €25–45 per person. A night in town with dinner and breakfast for two realistically lands between €120 and €200. Prices rise on summer weekends and during truffle season in autumn.

Typical per-person budgets:

- **Day trip from the coast (car, parking, lunch, wine, one purchase):** €25–45
- **Budget overnight (apartment, konoba dinner, self-catered breakfast):** €50–80
- **Mid-range overnight (guesthouse, two meals, wine):** €80–130
- **Higher-end weekend (boutique B&B, tasting dinners, truffle shopping):** €150+

One published estimate for a full week in the area is about €450–940 per person on a budget and €1,110–1,880 mid-range, flights excluded. Those figures include car hire and are a useful ceiling, since Grožnjan itself needs only one or two days.

## Accommodation Prices in Grožnjan

The town is tiny, so the supply is mostly private rooms, apartments, and a few boutique properties. Booking.com lists around 25 hotels and similar stays in the town itself, and the wider area (including villas in surrounding hamlets) has many more.

### Budget: €50–90 per night

Apartments and simple rooms are the best value. Lucky Home – Apartment Art Grožnjan and App Parenzana both score about 9.7/10 on Booking.com, with rates starting around €65–75 for two adults. Rooms Sara sits in the historic core, with air conditioning and Wi-Fi, and Tripadvisor shows rates from roughly €65–70. Rooms Svalina lists from €90 per night.

### Mid-range and boutique: €110–160 per night

B&B Artegnana 1798 and Ponte Porton Dining & lodging sit at the top end of local pricing, typically €130–145 per night for a double outside peak dates. Both include a restaurant, which cuts the need to drive after dinner.

### Villas with pools

Holiday homes and villas around Grožnjan generally cost €170–300+ per night for the whole property. They make sense for groups of four to eight, not for couples.

### Seasonal pricing

Typical averages sit near €100–115 per night, but weekend averages run noticeably higher, around €150–190. Autumn, especially October and November, is the busiest time because of white truffle season. Book at least a few weeks ahead for those months.

This is a place where staying overnight is worth the extra cost. Most visitors come for the day, and the town is at its best after the coaches leave, when the lanes are quiet.

## Food and Drink Costs

### Konobas and restaurants

Istrian konoba main courses (fuži or pljukanci pasta, grilled meat, boškarin beef) generally cost €14–25. Expect €25–35 per person with a starter, main, and a glass of local Malvazija. Truffle dishes add a substantial surcharge, often €10–25 per plate, because the truffle is weighed and charged separately.

Some local options include aModomio (a restaurant with valley views) and Sobe Pintur (rooms with a traditional Istrian restaurant in the centre). Bacchus Vinoteka at 1. svibnja 1 is a wine-focused stop. Hours differ by season, and some small places close between lunch and dinner or on weekdays in winter, so confirm before driving up.

### Truffle meals nearby

Motovun, about 20 km away, is the standard truffle destination. Konoba Pod Voltom there charges roughly €30–60 per person for a multi-course truffle meal, with mains typically €14–24 without truffle. Restaurant Zigante in Livade is the splurge option and needs several days' notice. The white truffle peak is October and November.

### Wine bar and shop

Zigante Enoteka at Gorjan 5 is a small wine bar and deli selling truffle products, cheeses, olive oils, and local wines, with seasonal hours that have been listed as daily 10:00–23:00 from May to October. A glass of wine with a snack costs about €5–12.

### Daily food budget

For planning, €20–60 per person per day covers everything from bakery breakfasts and picnic lunches to a sit-down dinner. Self-catering in a town this small is limited, so stock up at supermarkets in Buje (about 8 km) before arriving.

## Truffle Shopping and Souvenirs

Zigante Tartufi runs a shop in town selling truffle spreads, oils, salts, honey, and cheeses, and it offers tastings. Small jars of truffle products generally start around €8–15, while fresh truffles cost far more and fluctuate with the season. White truffles are priced by the gram and can reach several hundred euros per 100 g in peak weeks.

A tasting at the shop is a good way to decide what to buy. Compare prices with the shops in Buje and Motovun if you plan a large purchase.

The cheaper souvenirs are local olive oil, wine direct from small producers, and original work from the artist studios. Small prints and ceramics often cost €15–50.

## Transport and Parking

Grožnjan has no practical public transport for visitors, so a car is the realistic choice. Car rental typically costs €25–130 per day depending on the season and vehicle. Fuel and tolls from Poreč, Rovinj, or Umag add little, as the drive is short on regional roads.

The historic centre is pedestrian-focused. Park in the lots at the edge of the old town and walk in for a few minutes. Parking is generally modest in cost, with rates in the range of a few euros for several hours in season. Check posted signs for the current tariff, because rates and enforcement change by season.

The Parenzana trail, a former railway route used by cyclists, passes near the town. Bike rental in the area typically costs €15–30 per day. The climb into Grožnjan is steep, which makes an e-bike the better choice for anyone who is not a regular rider.

## Activities and Events

Walking the streets, visiting galleries, and viewing the valley cost nothing. Most studios are free to enter, and many are open mainly in summer. The town is known for music, and the Jeunesses Musicales International centre brings young musicians in summer, so free or low-cost concerts are common. Ticketed concerts and festival events typically cost in the €10–25 range, though prices vary by event.

The summer cultural season is the main reason to schedule a visit for July and August. The trade-off is heat and crowds.

## Money-Saving Tips

- **Eat lunch, not dinner, at the pricier places.** Many Istrian restaurants run cheaper lunch menus.
- **Choose a private apartment over a boutique B&B.** The price gap can be €50–80 per night.
- **Visit in late spring or early autumn.** Rates are lower than July–August or truffle weekends, and the weather is mild.
- **Skip the truffle plate unless it is the point of the trip.** The shaved-on-top dishes inflate bills quickly, and the shop jars give a similar flavour at much lower cost.
- **Carry some cash.** Small galleries and rural producers may not take cards.
- **Buy wine from producers near the town.** Bottles from small cellars are cheaper than in tourist shops.

The common advice to make Grožnjan a quick stop on a Motovun day trip sounds efficient, but it undersells the town. Two to three hours is enough to see the main street, though an evening here costs only slightly more than a hurried lunch and is worth it.

## Sample Budgets

| Traveler | Day trip | One night |
|---|---|---|
| Solo, budget | €25–35 | €60–90 |
| Couple, mid-range | €60–90 | €150–220 |
| Couple, truffle splurge | €100+ | €250+ |

## When to Visit for Best Value

June and early September usually give the best balance of open galleries, warm weather, and moderate rates. October and November are the best months for food but the most expensive for lodging and truffle dishes. Winter is cheapest, though many small businesses close or reduce hours.

faq.question: How much does a day trip to Grožnjan cost?
faq.answer: Plan on €25–45 per person for parking, lunch with a glass of wine, and a small purchase. Entry to the town and most galleries is free. Add fuel or car rental if you are driving from the coast.

faq.question: How much is a hotel or apartment in Grožnjan per night?
faq.answer: Budget apartments and rooms start around €50–90 per night. Boutique options such as B&B Artegnana 1798 run about €130–145. Weekends and truffle season push rates higher.

faq.question: Is Grožnjan expensive compared with Istrian coastal towns?
faq.answer: No. Lodging and meals are generally cheaper than in Rovinj or Poreč, particularly in summer. Truffle dishes and boutique stays are the main exceptions.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Grožnjan?
faq.answer: A konoba main course typically costs €14–25. A full meal with starter, main, and wine usually comes to €25–35 per person. Truffle dishes can add €10–25 per plate.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Grožnjan for lower prices?
faq.answer: Late spring and early September offer moderate rates and open businesses. October and November are the white truffle peak and cost the most. Winter is cheapest, but some places close.

faq.question: Do I need a car to visit Grožnjan?
faq.answer: Yes, for most visitors. Public transport is limited, and the town sits on a hill in the interior of Istria. Rental cars cost about €25–130 per day, depending on season.

faq.question: Are truffle products in Grožnjan worth buying?
faq.answer: Jars of truffle spreads, oils, and salts from the Zigante shop in town start around €8–15 and are the practical choice. Fresh truffles are far pricier and perishable. Taste before you buy.

quickAnswer: Grožnjan is moderately priced for Istria. Budget about €25–45 per person for a day trip with lunch and wine. Rooms in town usually cost €60–100 per night for two, and a konoba main course runs roughly €14–25. Truffle products and summer weekends push costs higher.
